sexual-consent / legal-age / relationships node (Thread B · Safety, Consent & Boundaries) at its adult peak.
"Intimacy is mutual or it is nothing." 84 researched, India-grounded, even-handed, never-explicit scenarios
across what-consent-is → reading-respecting → pressure-coercion → the-mutual-zone → rights-and-law →
mutual-respect-equal, each encoded as one of the shared v2 play actions (reflect / strike-rewrite / branch /

title: Mutual
greet: I’m Lensy. 💞 Intimacy is mutual, or it’s nothing: a clear, willing, enthusiastic ‘yes’ from both, every time, and either of you can change your mind.

badge.title: Mutual Respect 💞
badge.blurb: You know consent: FRIES (freely given, reversible, informed, enthusiastic, specific). A real ‘yes’ from both, withdrawable anytime. You respect a no. 🤝

helpLine: If anyone pressures you or crosses a line, it is never your fault. Reach Women Helpline 181, women-in-distress 1091, emergency 112, or Childline 1098.
reassure: Consent is a free yes from both, takeable back anytime. If someone won’t take no, that’s on them, never you. You can always stop and get help (181 / 1098). 💞

scenarios.hook: "Consent just means the other person didn't say no."

myth.un: Consent means no one said 'no'.
myth.re: Consent is the presence of a clear, willing 'yes', not the absence of a 'no'.
myth.why: Silence or freezing is not agreement.

scenarios.relearn: Consent is a clear, willing 'yes', not just the absence of 'no'.

scenarios.hook: "Once you've said yes, you can't change your mind."

myth.un: Once you say yes, you can't take it back.
myth.re: Consent is reversible; either person can stop at any moment.
myth.why: Changing your mind is always allowed.

scenarios.relearn: Consent is reversible; you can stop at any moment.

scenarios.hook: "Saying yes to one thing means yes to everything."

myth.un: Yes to one thing is yes to everything.
myth.re: Consent is specific; agreeing to one thing isn't agreeing to all.
myth.why: Each step needs its own willing yes.

scenarios.relearn: Consent is specific; one yes isn't a yes to everything.

scenarios.hook: "If they're just going along with it, that counts."

myth.un: Going along with it counts as consent.
myth.re: Consent is enthusiastic, both people actively want it, not just tolerate it.
myth.why: Reluctant 'okay' isn't a willing yes.

scenarios.relearn: Consent is enthusiastic; tolerating isn't the same as wanting.

scenarios.hook: "Consent doesn't need real information."

myth.un: You don't need the full picture to consent.
myth.re: Consent is informed; a yes based on a lie (like a removed condom) isn't real consent.
myth.why: You can only agree to what you actually know.

scenarios.relearn: Consent is informed; a yes based on a lie isn't consent.

scenarios.hook: You and Meera are sitting close on her terrace after her cousin's mehendi.

steps.prompt: You'd like to kiss her, but you can't tell if she wants to. What do you do?

options.text: Lean in slowly and see if she leans in too
options.then: She turns her head a little. You can't tell if that was a no.

options.text: Pause and ask: "Do you want to?"
options.then: Meera smiles, surprised. "Not yet. Can we just talk for now?"

options.text: Assume she does, since she came up here with you
options.then: You lean in. She turns her face away, suddenly awkward.

options.text: Ask a friend tomorrow whether Meera likes you
options.then: The moment passes. You still don't know what Meera wants.

steps.why: When you're unsure, asking is the only way to know. Guessing isn't enough.

steps.prompt: Later your friend Rohit says asking first kills the mood. What do you say?

options.text: Agree, and plan to just read the signs next time
options.then: Rohit nods. You feel less sure of yourself than before.

options.text: Laugh it off and change the subject
options.then: Rohit keeps talking about 'smooth moves' all the way home.

options.text: Say asking is part of it, and makes it better
options.then: Rohit rolls his eyes, then admits he's never actually asked anyone.

options.text: Tell him only a creep would never ask
options.then: Rohit gets defensive, and the chat turns into an argument.

steps.why: Checking in is normal and warm. It's part of closeness, not a mood-killer.

steps.prompt: A week later you and Meera hold hands at the movies. You'd like to put an arm around her. What do you do?

options.text: Do it, since holding hands was already fine
options.then: She goes a little still, and you can't tell why.

options.text: Stretch and slide your arm over, casually
options.then: She glances at your arm, then back at the screen.

options.text: Whisper, "Okay if I put my arm around you?"
options.then: She shifts closer. "Yes. Thanks for asking."

options.text: Don't. Asking twice in one week feels like too much
options.then: Your arm stays put, and so does the question.

steps.why: Yes to one thing isn't yes to everything. A quick ask keeps it mutual.

scenarios.debrief: When unsure, checking in is always the caring move.
scenarios.relearn: If you're unsure, pause and check in, never assume.

scenarios.hook: You and Farhan are kissing on a quiet bench by the lake after tuition.

steps.prompt: Farhan suddenly pulls back and says, "Wait." What do you do?

options.text: Ask: "Why? Did I do something wrong?"
options.then: Farhan looks unsure. "No, I just..." He trails off.

options.text: Stop right away and give him some space
options.then: Farhan lets out a breath. "Thanks. I just needed a second."

options.text: Stop, but sigh so he knows you're let down
options.then: Farhan hears the sigh. "Okay, never mind," he says, looking away.

options.text: Slow down but stay close, and keep going
options.then: Farhan leans away again, more firmly this time.

steps.why: "Wait" means stop now, with no questions and no sulking.

steps.prompt: A few minutes later, Farhan says he's okay but would rather just sit and talk. What do you do?

options.text: Say, "Sure. We can pick up where we left off later"
options.then: Farhan's smile fades a little. "Maybe," he says.

options.text: Sit back and talk, happy just to be with him
options.then: Farhan relaxes and starts telling you about his week.

options.text: Check your phone until he seems ready again
options.then: Farhan watches you scroll and goes quiet too.

options.text: Ask him to explain exactly what he didn't like
options.then: Farhan shifts. "I don't know. Can we not do this now?"

steps.why: Respecting a stop means letting it be, with no plan to restart.

steps.prompt: That evening your friend Aisha bets you were annoyed when he said wait. What do you say?

options.text: "A bit. He could have said it earlier."
options.then: Aisha shrugs. "People don't always know earlier."

options.text: "Yeah. It was kind of embarrassing for me."
options.then: Aisha laughs. "Embarrassing? For you?"

options.text: "Whatever. I'll be pickier about who I date."
options.then: Aisha frowns. "Because he said wait?"

options.text: "No. I'm glad he felt he could say it."
options.then: Aisha smiles. "Fair. That's actually sweet."

steps.why: A stop is something to welcome. It means they trust you to hear it.

scenarios.debrief: A boundary, once said, is honoured instantly, with no negotiation.
scenarios.relearn: 'Stop' means stop immediately, no questions, no sulking.

scenarios.hook: On the bus back from the school trip, you rest your head on Aarav's shoulder.
scenarios.setup: Halfway home, the bus goes quiet.

steps.prompt: Aarav shifts and says: "Sorry, my shoulder's a bit stiff."

options.text: "You're fine, right?"
options.then: "Yeah, fine," he says, still stiff.

options.text: "Is this okay? I can move anytime."
options.then: He smiles. "Maybe lean on my other side?"

options.text: "Oh. Never mind, then."
options.then: "No, it's not that," he says, but you've already moved.

options.text: "Just relax. It's comfy."
options.then: He tries, but his arm stays tense.

steps.why: A warm "Is this okay?" makes it easy for him to say what he needs.

steps.prompt: Later Aarav says: "My cousin says asking 'is this okay?' kills the mood. Does it?"

options.text: "A bit. But I'd rather be safe."
options.then: He nods. "Safe. Right." It sounds like a rule.

options.text: "No. It's how I know we both want it."
options.then: "Huh," he says. "I like that, actually."

options.text: "Yeah. Asking makes things awkward."
options.then: "Does it?" he asks, rubbing his stiff shoulder.

options.text: "Only once. Asking again would be too much."
options.then: He thinks. "But what if things change?"

steps.why: Checking in is caring, not awkward. It's how a yes stays shared.

steps.prompt: As you get off the bus, Aarav asks: "Sit together on the next trip too?"

options.text: "Sure. I'll just lean whenever. You'll get used to it."
options.then: He hesitates. "Maybe still ask first?"

options.text: "Yes. And just tell me if anything feels off."
options.then: Aarav smiles. "I will. And I'll ask you too."

options.text: "Only if your shoulder behaves this time."
options.then: He laughs, but his smile slips a little.

options.text: "Yes. If something's off, I'll figure it out."
options.then: He nods, unsure how you'd know.

steps.why: Inviting him to speak up makes comfort a two-way thing, every time.

scenarios.relearn: 'Is this okay? We can stop anytime' is caring, not unromantic.

scenarios.hook: At a cousin's sangeet, you and Rohan are kissing on the terrace. After a while, you want to stop.
scenarios.setup: The music from downstairs drifts up.

steps.prompt: Rohan whispers: "This is nice. I'm glad we came up here."

options.text: "I guess I should be fine with this by now."
options.then: Rohan pauses. "Should? Wait. Are you not fine?"

options.text: "I want to stop now. I'm not comfortable."
options.then: Rohan pulls back at once. "Okay. Sorry. Are you alright?"

options.text: "Sorry. I'm being weird. Ignore me."
options.then: Rohan stops. "Weird how? You've gone really still."

options.text: "Can't you tell I'm not into this?"
options.then: Rohan pulls back, flustered. "Sorry. I couldn't tell."

steps.why: Saying "I want to stop" plainly is clear and fair. It needs no apology.

steps.prompt: Rohan sits back and asks: "Was I going too fast? Tell me honestly."

options.text: "No, no. It's all my fault, honestly."
options.then: He frowns. "Fault? Wanting to stop isn't a fault."

options.text: "A bit. I'd like to stop and just sit for now."
options.then: He nods and shifts back. "Okay. Sitting is good."

options.text: "Maybe. Anyone else would be fine with it, though."
options.then: He shakes his head. "I don't care about anyone else."

options.text: "No. I'll get used to going faster, promise."
options.then: He hesitates. "You shouldn't have to get used to it."

steps.why: Wanting to stop is never a fault. Saying it plainly lets him respect it.

steps.prompt: Downstairs, your cousin Mehak whispers: "Why did you come down? Rohan's so cute!"

options.text: "I know. I probably ruined it."
options.then: Mehak shrugs. "He'll get over it."

options.text: "Maybe I should go back up and say sorry."
options.then: Mehak tilts her head. "Up to you. He did look a bit sad."

options.text: "You go up, then. You think he's so cute."
options.then: Mehak laughs awkwardly. "I was only joking."

options.text: "I wanted to stop. That's reason enough."
options.then: Mehak blinks. "Huh. I wish I could say it that easily."

steps.why: Wanting to stop is reason enough. You never owe anyone an explanation.

steps.prompt: Later Rohan texts: "Can we hang out again? Slower this time."

options.text: "Sure. Next time you decide how far we go."
options.then: "Me?" he replies. "I'd rather we decide together."

options.text: "Sorry about tonight. I'll be better."
options.then: "Better at what?" he replies.

options.text: "I'd like that. Let's both say what feels okay."
options.then: "Deal," he replies. "And I'll keep asking."

options.text: "Yes. And I won't make a fuss next time."
options.then: "Okay," he replies, and you wonder what you just promised.

steps.why: Agreeing you'll both speak up keeps any yes shared, every time.

scenarios.relearn: You can clearly say 'I want to stop', and it must be respected.

scenarios.hook: You and Neha are holding hands on her sofa, and she leans in for a kiss.
scenarios.setup: The film is paused in the background.

steps.prompt: She stops just short and asks softly: "Is this okay?"

options.text: "Sorry. I'm just bad at this stuff."
options.then: "You're not bad at anything," she says, still close.

options.text: "Why do you keep asking me that?"
options.then: Neha pulls back, hurt. "I just wanted to check."

options.text: "Can we slow down? I'm not sure yet."
options.then: She smiles and sits back. "Of course. Thanks for saying."

options.text: "Maybe after the film ends?"
options.then: "Okay," she says. "After the film, then."

steps.why: "I'm not sure yet" is a complete answer. You can always ask to slow down.

steps.prompt: Neha asks gently: "Be honest. Am I rushing you?"

options.text: "No. I'm just not sure yet. That's all."
options.then: She nods. "Then we wait. Tell me anytime."

options.text: "A little. You always rush things."
options.then: Neha's face falls. "Always?"

options.text: "No. It's my fault for being so slow."
options.then: "Slow isn't a fault," she says gently.

options.text: "Kind of. But I'll catch up soon, promise."
options.then: "There's nothing to catch up on," she says, frowning.

steps.why: Saying where you are, without blaming either of you, keeps it easy.

steps.prompt: Next day your friend Tara says: "If someone asks 'is this okay?', I just say yes. Easier."

options.text: "Same. Saying anything else just makes it weird."
options.then: Tara grins. "Right? Why make a fuss?"

options.text: "Then it's not a real yes. 'Not sure' counts too."
options.then: Tara pauses. "Huh. Maybe I should try that."

options.text: "Real couples don't even need to ask, honestly."
options.then: Tara frowns. "Wait. That sounds worse."

options.text: "Easier, sure. Whatever works for you."
options.then: Tara shrugs and changes the subject.

steps.why: A yes only counts if it's real. 'Not sure yet' is a full answer.

scenarios.relearn: You can ask to slow down; 'I'm not sure yet' is a complete answer.

scenarios.hook: "Asking 'is this okay?' ruins the moment."

myth.un: Checking in ruins the mood.
myth.re: Checking in is caring and attractive; it makes both people feel safe.
myth.why: Respect adds to intimacy, it doesn't subtract.

scenarios.relearn: Checking in is caring and adds to intimacy, never ruins it.

scenarios.hook: At the mall, Zoya lets go of your hand. She says hand-holding in public isn't for her.

steps.prompt: You feel a sting of disappointment. What do you do?

options.text: Say "Okay," then go quiet for the next hour
options.then: Zoya keeps glancing at you, unsure what she did.

options.text: Ask: "Are you embarrassed to be seen with me?"
options.then: Zoya looks stricken. "No! It's not that at all."

options.text: Say "Okay" warmly, and keep walking together
options.then: Zoya relaxes and bumps your shoulder as you walk.

options.text: Joke, "Fine, but you owe me at the cinema"
options.then: Zoya laughs, but it sounds a little forced.

steps.why: You can feel disappointed and still respect her boundary fully.

steps.prompt: On the bus home, the disappointment is still there. What do you do with it?

options.text: Text Zoya that it hurt, so she knows how you feel
options.then: Zoya replies, "Sorry," and then, "Should I just do it?"

options.text: Let yourself feel it, and let it pass
options.then: By your stop, the sting has faded and you're texting her about the film.

options.text: Scroll through couples' photos online
options.then: Every picture of a couple holding hands makes the sting sharper.

options.text: Decide she must not like you that much
options.then: The thought follows you all the way home.

steps.why: Your feelings are yours to handle. They don't get to push her boundary.

steps.prompt: A few days later Zoya asks if the hand thing felt weird for you. What do you say?

options.text: "Not at all. It didn't bother me one bit."
options.then: Zoya nods, but she doesn't quite look like she believes you.

options.text: "Kind of. Maybe you could try it just once?"
options.then: Zoya's smile slips. "I said it's not for me."

options.text: "It's fine. My last partner held hands everywhere, though."
options.then: Zoya goes quiet. "Okay. Good for them."

options.text: "A little, at first. But I want you comfortable."
options.then: Zoya smiles. "Thanks for being honest. I like that you get it."

steps.why: An honest feeling, without asking her to change, keeps trust.

steps.prompt: At a friend's birthday, someone teases that you two never hold hands. What do you do?

options.text: Say, "We're good as we are," and move on
options.then: The teasing fizzles. Zoya catches your eye, grateful.

options.text: Laugh and say, "Ask her. It's her rule."
options.then: Everyone turns to Zoya, who goes red.

options.text: Grab her hand as a joke to shut them up
options.then: Zoya pulls her hand back fast and looks away.

options.text: Explain her reasons to the whole group
options.then: Zoya winces as everyone turns to look at her.

steps.why: Backing her boundary in front of others shows respect when it counts.

scenarios.debrief: You can feel disappointed and still fully respect a boundary.
scenarios.relearn: Respect a boundary even when you feel disappointed.

scenarios.hook: You and Aman are kissing on the sofa during a film at his place.

steps.prompt: You notice Aman has gone quiet and still. What do you do?

options.text: Take the quiet as a yes and carry on
options.then: Aman doesn't move or kiss you back.

options.text: Kiss him more gently to see if he warms up
options.then: Aman turns his face slightly away.

options.text: Pause and ask softly: "You okay?"
options.then: Aman exhales. "I just felt a bit weird. Can we stop?"

options.text: Stop and ask: "What's wrong with you tonight?"
options.then: Aman flushes. "Nothing. Forget it."

steps.why: Quiet and stillness can mean discomfort. Pausing to check is caring.

steps.prompt: A few minutes later, the film is still on and Aman hasn't said much. What do you do?

options.text: Keep asking him if he's sure he's okay
options.then: "I said I'm fine," Aman says, sounding tired.

options.text: Go quiet yourself and scroll your phone
options.then: The silence stretches until the credits roll.

options.text: Suggest you try again once the film ends
options.then: Aman nods without looking at you.

options.text: Give him space and say there's no rush at all
options.then: Aman settles back and, after a while, laughs at a scene.

steps.why: Making it clear nothing is expected helps him feel safe again.

steps.prompt: Next day Aman texts, "Sorry about last night. I froze." What do you reply?

options.text: "It's okay. Just tell me next time, though."
options.then: Aman replies, "I'll try," and nothing more.

options.text: "No need to say sorry. I'm glad we stopped."
options.then: Aman replies with a long row of hearts.

options.text: "Yeah, it was kind of awkward for me too."
options.then: Aman leaves you on read for an hour.

options.text: "Don't worry. We'll make up for it soon."
options.then: "Sure," Aman replies, after a long pause.

steps.why: Freezing is never his fault. Reassurance with no conditions keeps trust.

scenarios.debrief: Silence isn't a yes. A check-in is the caring response.
scenarios.relearn: Silence or stillness isn't a yes; pause and check in.

scenarios.hook: You put your arm around Joel at the movies. He pulls away and goes stiff.
scenarios.setup: The film is still playing.

steps.prompt: Joel whispers: "Um. Can you not?"

options.text: "Oh. I thought you'd like it."
options.then: Joel shrinks. "I know. Sorry."

options.text: "Sorry. I misread that. You okay?"
options.then: Joel nods. "Yeah. Just not in public."

options.text: "Fine. I won't touch you, then."
options.then: Joel stares at the screen, miserable.

options.text: "Shh. The best part is coming up."
options.then: Joel stays stiff for the rest of the film.

steps.why: A quick, simple sorry and a check-in repairs it without fuss.

steps.prompt: After the film, Joel says: "I'm not really into touching in public."

options.text: "Why not? Nobody's even looking at us."
options.then: Joel shrugs. "It's still how I feel."

options.text: "Are you embarrassed to be seen with me?"
options.then: Joel sighs. "It's not about you."

options.text: "Thanks for telling me. I'll remember."
options.then: Joel relaxes. "Okay. I was worried you'd be upset."

options.text: "Okay, but you could have told me before."
options.then: Joel looks at his shoes. "I didn't think of it."

steps.why: Welcoming a boundary, with no questions, makes the next one easier to share.

steps.prompt: On the walk home, Joel asks: "Are we okay?"

options.text: "Yeah. Just don't make it a thing again."
options.then: Joel's face falls. "Okay."

options.text: "Sure. I'll never touch you again, promise."
options.then: Joel laughs nervously. "That's not what I said."

options.text: "Depends. Are you always going to be like this?"
options.then: Joel goes quiet. "Like what?"

options.text: "We're good. I'd rather ask than guess."
options.then: Joel grins and bumps your shoulder.

steps.why: Reassuring him, and choosing to ask next time, is how repair lasts.

scenarios.relearn: If you misread a cue, stop, apologise simply, and check they're okay.

myth.why: Pressure removes the 'freely given' part.

myth.un: 'If you loved me, you would.'

scenarios.relearn: 'If you loved me' is guilt-based pressure, not love.

scenarios.hook: "Being in a relationship (or married) means you've already agreed."

myth.un: A relationship or marriage means standing consent.
myth.re: Consent is needed every time; a relationship never means automatic yes.
myth.why: No status removes the right to choose each time.

scenarios.hook: You've told your partner Ritvik you're not ready, but he keeps bringing it up.

steps.prompt: He brings it up again at the bus stop. What do you do?

options.text: Wonder if you're being unfair to him
options.then: The thought follows you home. You feel guilty for having a no.

options.text: Explain your reasons once more, in detail
options.then: Ritvik picks apart each reason. It turns into a debate.

options.text: Hold your no. The pushing is the problem, not you
options.then: Ritvik sighs loudly. "Fine. For now," he says.

options.text: Decide the pushing shows how much he loves you
options.then: You feel flattered for a moment. The pushing carries on.

steps.why: Repeated pushing is the problem. Your no is complete as it is.

steps.prompt: That week, a friend says you should just 'get it over with' to keep him. What do you think?

options.text: Maybe your friend is right about keeping him
options.then: The idea worries you all evening.

options.text: No one owes intimacy to keep a relationship
options.then: Your friend shrugs. Saying it out loud makes you feel steadier.

options.text: Maybe everyone your age has already done it
options.then: You start doubting your own no.

options.text: Ask your friend to talk to Ritvik for you
options.then: Your friend tells Ritvik. He's annoyed you talked about him.

steps.why: A relationship never earns a yes. Your no stands by itself.

steps.prompt: Ritvik starts going cold whenever you say no. What do you do?

options.text: Decide his coldness means you're failing him
options.then: You spend the week apologising for things you didn't do.

options.text: Ask his friends what's wrong with him
options.then: His friends tell him. He's angry you 'gossiped'.

options.text: Tell yourself all couples go through this
options.then: You wave it off. The coldness keeps happening.

options.text: Talk to a trusted adult about it
options.then: The counsellor listens and says the pushing is his to stop, not yours to fix.

steps.why: A trusted adult can help you hold your no. This is never your fault.

steps.prompt: A week later, Ritvik says sorry and asks to start fresh. What do you do?

options.text: Accept, and promise to be less difficult
options.then: Ritvik smiles. You've taken on blame that was never yours.

options.text: Say a fresh start means no more pushing, ever
options.then: Ritvik nods. You watch how he acts, and keep a trusted adult in the loop.

options.text: Believe his sorry means it won't happen again
options.then: You relax, and stop telling anyone how things are going.

options.text: Ask him to prove he's changed by waiting a month
options.then: Ritvik agrees. Now your no has an end date.

steps.why: Naming the terms is fair. Whether he keeps them is on him, never on you.

scenarios.debrief: Repeated pushing past a 'no' is coercion; holding your no is right.
scenarios.relearn: Hold your 'no'; someone pushing past it is the problem.

scenarios.hook: You'd like things to go further with Sahil, but he seems hesitant.

steps.prompt: You feel the urge to ask again, just once more. What do you do?

options.text: Ask once more, but nicely this time
options.then: Sahil says "maybe" and looks at the floor.

options.text: Stop, and treat his hesitation as a no for now
options.then: Sahil relaxes a little and talks more freely the rest of the evening.

options.text: Push a little. He'll probably come round
options.then: Sahil goes quiet and pulls his hand back.

options.text: Sulk a bit so he knows you're disappointed
options.then: Sahil apologises, though he's done nothing wrong.

steps.why: Hesitation is a no for now. Stopping keeps you someone he can trust.

steps.prompt: Later, you wonder if Sahil just needs some encouragement. What do you do with that thought?

options.text: Plan a romantic evening to get him in the mood
options.then: You plan it all, built around getting a yes.

options.text: Ask his best friend what he really wants
options.then: His friend shrugs. Now someone else is in your business.

options.text: See that 'encouragement' here would be pressure
options.then: You let it go. The urge fades by the time you get home.

options.text: Decide he's just not that into you
options.then: You pull back. Sahil can't tell why you've gone cold.

steps.why: Waiting for a free yes means not building pressure, even gently.

steps.prompt: A week later Sahil asks what you'd do if he's not ready for a long while. What do you say?

options.text: Ask how long 'a long while' means
options.then: Sahil shifts. "I don't know. Does it need a date?"

options.text: Say you'd wait, with a disappointed sigh
options.then: Sahil hears the sigh and goes quiet.

options.text: Say you'd start to wonder about the relationship
options.then: Sahil's face tightens. It sounds like a warning.

options.text: Say then you'll wait, and it's his call
options.then: Sahil smiles. "Okay. That takes a weight off."

steps.why: Making clear there's no rush lets his yes be free, whenever it comes.

scenarios.debrief: Being even-handed means checking your own behaviour too.
scenarios.relearn: Treat a partner's hesitation as no-for-now; don't pressure it.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Pallavi says her boyfriend keeps pressuring her, and she feels she has to give in.

steps.prompt: She looks at you, waiting. What do you say first?

options.text: Tell her to keep the peace. It's easier that way
options.then: Pallavi nods slowly. She looks more trapped than before.

options.text: Ask her why she's still with him, then
options.then: Pallavi stiffens. "It's not that simple," she says.

options.text: Say a pressured yes isn't owed, and you're with her
options.then: Pallavi's eyes fill. "I thought I was being dramatic."

options.text: Say you'll go and tell him off yourself
options.then: Pallavi panics. "Please don't. It'll get worse."

steps.why: Believing her, and saying nothing is owed, takes the guilt off her.

steps.prompt: Pallavi asks you to promise not to tell anyone. What do you say?

options.text: Say you can't promise that, but you'll stay with her
options.then: Pallavi hesitates. "Okay. Just don't do anything without me."

options.text: Promise, since it's her story to tell
options.then: Pallavi hugs you. You carry it home alone, worried, all night.

options.text: Say you'll tell her parents tonight, whatever she says
options.then: Pallavi goes pale. "No. Please, not like this," she begs. You hold off for tonight.

options.text: Agree it's best kept quiet so it doesn't spread
options.then: Pallavi nods. The pressure stays hidden.

steps.why: You can't keep a secret that leaves her at risk, but you can stay beside her.

steps.prompt: Next day at break, Pallavi says she's not ready to tell anyone at home. What do you do?

options.text: Drop it until she brings it up again herself
options.then: Days pass. Pallavi seems more and more tired.

options.text: Tell her she has to go to the police today
options.then: Pallavi shuts down. "I can't. Forget I said anything."

options.text: Give her Childline 1098 and leave it at that
options.then: Pallavi saves the number, but doesn't feel ready to call alone.

options.text: Suggest the counsellor, and offer to go with her
options.then: Pallavi thinks, then nods. "If you come, I'll try."

steps.why: A trusted adult, at her pace and with you beside her, is real support.

steps.prompt: A week later, Pallavi says he got angry when she said no. What do you do?

options.text: Tell her she has to break up with him, right now
options.then: Pallavi bristles. "You don't get it," she says, and walks off.

options.text: Say it isn't her fault. Offer Childline 1098 together
options.then: Pallavi breathes out. "Okay. Can we call at lunch?"

options.text: Suggest she apologise to him, so he calms down
options.then: Pallavi looks unsure, then slowly shakes her head.

options.text: Ask her what she did to make him so angry
options.then: Pallavi looks at the floor. "Nothing. I just said no."

steps.why: His anger is his responsibility. It's never her fault, and help is there.

steps.prompt: Later, Pallavi says she feels stupid for not saying no sooner. What do you say?

options.text: Say that next time she should say no straight away
options.then: Pallavi nods, but looks more ashamed.

options.text: Say everyone makes mistakes in relationships
options.then: Pallavi winces. "So it was a mistake?"

options.text: Change the subject and offer to get chai
options.then: Pallavi smiles a little. The shame stays unspoken.

options.text: Say she's not stupid. His pressure is never her fault
options.then: Pallavi wipes her eyes. "Thank you. I needed that."

steps.why: Lifting self-blame matters. Pressure is always on the one applying it.

scenarios.debrief: Friends can remind each other that no one owes intimacy, and pressure is never their fault.
scenarios.relearn: Support a pressured friend: a pressured yes is never owed.

scenarios.hook: Your partner Ayaan hints he'll spread rumours about you, or break up, unless you agree.

steps.prompt: He says it like a joke, but he means it. What do you do?

options.text: Tell yourself it's just how he jokes
options.then: You laugh it off. He makes the same 'joke' the next day.

options.text: See it as a threat, and refuse
options.then: Ayaan's smile drops. "Fine. Your loss," he says.

options.text: Try to reason with him about why it's unfair
options.then: Ayaan argues every point. The threat is still there.

options.text: Decide you must have led him on somehow
options.then: You feel guilty all evening for something that's his doing.

steps.why: Naming a threat as a threat is the first step. A yes under threat isn't consent.

steps.prompt: That night you can't sleep for thinking about it. What do you do?

options.text: Search online for how to stop rumours
options.then: You read for hours and feel more alone, not less.

options.text: Tell yourself breakups happen, so it's no big deal
options.then: You try to shrug it off. The threat about rumours stays.

options.text: Tell someone you trust, like your mum or the counsellor
options.then: Your mum listens calmly. "This is not your fault. We'll handle it together."

options.text: Message his friends to get them on your side first
options.then: His friends screenshot it to him. He's angrier now.

steps.why: Telling a trusted adult means you don't face a threat alone. It's never your fault.

steps.prompt: Next day, Ayaan messages: 'Last chance. Everyone will hear about you.' What do you do?

options.text: Save the messages, and show a trusted adult
options.then: Your aunt reads them, and you work out next steps together.

options.text: Delete the messages so no one sees them
options.then: The threat is gone from your phone, but not from his.

options.text: Reply with a threat of your own
options.then: Ayaan screenshots it and sends it around.

options.text: Believe that if rumours spread, it'll be your fault
options.then: You feel ashamed before anything has even happened.

steps.why: Saved messages help an adult act. A threat is always on the person making it.

steps.prompt: A few days later, you hear Ayaan has done this to someone else too. What do you do?

options.text: Keep out of it. It's not really your business
options.then: The other person faces it alone.

options.text: Post a warning about Ayaan on your story
options.then: The post spreads, and Ayaan sends you new threats.

options.text: Tell them it's partly their fault for dating him
options.then: They go quiet and stop talking to you.

options.text: Tell a trusted adult, so others can be protected too
options.then: The counsellor thanks you and says she'll look into it carefully.

steps.why: Telling an adult can protect others too. Threats are on the one making them.

scenarios.debrief: Threats and blackmail are coercion; refusing and telling someone is right.
scenarios.relearn: Threats to make you agree are coercion; refuse and tell someone.

scenarios.hook: Your partner Mansi turns to guilt when you say no to going further.

options.then: Mansi nods slowly. "A little bit, yeah."

options.text: "Let me explain exactly why, so you understand."
options.then: Mansi folds her arms. "Go on, then. Convince me."

options.text: "Then maybe you should date one of them."
options.then: Mansi flinches. "Wow."

options.text: "Maybe it is normal to give in sometimes."
options.then: Mansi nods eagerly. "Exactly."

options.text: "What others do doesn't change my answer."
options.then: Mansi goes quiet. "Fine. I just feel rejected."

steps.why: Comparison is pressure in disguise. Your answer belongs to you.

steps.prompt: Later, your mum asks: "You've been quiet all evening. What's going on?"

options.text: "Mansi's upset with me. I think I'm a terrible partner."
options.then: Your mum frowns. "Terrible? What's been happening?"

options.text: "Mansi keeps guilt-tripping me. Can I talk to you?"

options.text: "Everyone says couples guilt each other. It's normal."
options.then: "Is it?" your mum asks. "Tell me more."

options.text: "Mansi says I should try harder. Maybe she's right."
options.then: Your mum looks up. "Try harder at what, exactly?"

steps.why: Talking to a trusted adult helps. Being guilt-tripped is never your fault.

scenarios.relearn: You can name guilt-tripping and keep your 'no'.

scenarios.hook: Pranav asks you back to his place after the film. You don't want to go.
scenarios.setup: It's still early, and the street outside is busy and bright.

steps.prompt: Pranav asks: "So, my place? My parents are out."

options.text: "I'm so sorry. I really wish I could, but..."
options.then: Pranav smiles. "So maybe next time?"

options.text: "I can't. I've got a test tomorrow."
options.then: "After the test, then?" Pranav asks hopefully.

options.text: "No. I don't want to, and that's enough."
options.then: Pranav blinks. "Oh. Okay. Can I ask why?"

options.text: "Ew, no. Why would I want that?"
options.then: Pranav's face falls. "Okay. No need to be mean."

steps.why: A plain no is a complete answer. It needs no excuse and no apology.

steps.prompt: Pranav asks: "Is it something I did?"

options.text: "No. I just don't want to, and that's okay."
options.then: Pranav nods. "Fair. Ice cream instead?"

options.text: "Not really. Maybe ask me on a better day."
options.then: Pranav brightens. "Okay. When's a better day?"

options.text: "No, no. I'm just weird about this stuff. Sorry."
options.then: Pranav laughs awkwardly. "You're not weird."

options.text: "Let me explain everything properly."
options.then: Pranav listens, then picks at your reasons one by one.

steps.prompt: Pranav asks: "Maybe another weekend, then?"

options.then: Pranav grins. "I'll hold you to that."

options.text: "I'm really sorry. I feel so bad saying no."
options.then: Pranav softens. "Don't feel bad. So is that a maybe?"

options.text: "Maybe not. If that changes, I'll tell you."
options.then: Pranav nods. "Okay. You'll tell me."

options.text: "Ask me again next week and we'll see."
options.then: Pranav smiles. "Okay. I'll keep asking, then."

steps.why: Leaving the next step to you keeps your no clear, with no promise attached.

scenarios.relearn: 'No, and that's enough' is a complete answer, no over-explaining needed.

scenarios.hook: Your partner Nisha decides every plan for the two of you, and you want an equal say.
scenarios.setup: Tonight she calls while you're doing homework.

steps.prompt: Nisha says: "Saturday's sorted. Mall at four, then my cousin's place."

options.text: "Sounds great. Whatever you want is fine by me."
options.then: "Perfect," Nisha says, already planning Sunday.

options.text: "Maybe next time I could at least pick the time?"
options.then: "Sure," she says. Next time she picks everything but the time.

options.text: "You always do this. You're so bossy."
options.then: Nisha bristles. "Bossy? I'm the one doing all the work."

options.text: "Can we decide the big stuff together, as equals?"
options.then: Nisha pauses. "Oh. I thought you liked me handling it."

steps.why: Asking plainly to decide together names the issue and opens the door.

steps.prompt: Next day, Nisha asks: "Be honest. Do you mind me deciding everything?"

options.text: "No, it's fine. It's easier this way."
options.then: "Great," she says. You feel yourself go quiet.

options.text: "I do, a bit. I want my say to count too."
options.then: "Okay," Nisha says slowly. "What would you want on Saturday?"

options.text: "Yes. So I'll decide everything for a month."
options.then: Nisha laughs uneasily. "That's not really better, is it?"

options.text: "I don't know. Whatever keeps us happy."
options.then: "Okay," Nisha says, relieved, and the plans stay hers.

steps.why: Being honest that it matters gives her the chance to share decisions.

steps.prompt: A week later, Nisha asks: "How do you think we should decide plans?"

options.text: "You decide, but run it past me first."
options.then: "Fine," she says. You're still only approving her plans.

options.text: "We'll take turns being in charge."
options.then: "Fair," Nisha says, though one of you is still always in charge.

options.text: "We each say what we want, then choose together."
options.then: Nisha smiles. "Okay. Mall, then your pick after?"

options.text: "Let's not make rules. It'll work itself out."
options.then: Nisha shrugs. By next week, she's planning everything again.

steps.why: Choosing together, not taking turns in charge, keeps power equal.

scenarios.relearn: Naming 'let's decide together' resets the relationship to equal footing.

scenarios.hook: On the walk home, your friend Manav says he just wears people down till they say yes.
scenarios.setup: He grins, waiting for you to laugh.

steps.prompt: Manav says: "Works every time. You should try it."

options.text: "A worn-down yes isn't a yes. That's not respect."
options.then: Manav frowns. "Come on. It's not that serious."

options.text: "Ha. Maybe I will, then. What's the trick?"
options.then: "Trust me," Manav says, pleased, and starts giving you tips.

options.text: "Anyway. Did you see the match last night?"
options.then: Manav talks cricket for a bit, then grins. "But seriously, try it."

options.text: "Seriously? That's so gross. You're actually gross."
options.then: Manav laughs it off. "Relax. You're way too sensitive."

steps.why: Naming wearing down as not-consent strips the joke of its cover.

steps.prompt: Manav goes on: "It's like in films. Persistence is romantic."

options.text: "Yeah, true. Films do make it look romantic."
options.then: "Exactly," Manav says. "It's romance."

options.text: "Okay, but maybe don't do it quite so much."
options.then: Manav grins. "So a little is fine?"

options.text: "Whatever. I honestly don't care what you do."
options.then: "Cool," Manav says, a bit thrown by your shrug.

options.text: "Films aren't consent. Pushing past no is pressure."
options.then: Manav goes quiet. "Huh. I never thought about the films."

steps.why: Persistence past a no is pressure, however films dress it up.

steps.prompt: Manav asks: "So what would you do if someone said no to you?"

options.text: "Ask again later, but more nicely."
options.then: Manav brightens. "So, persistence, but polite."

options.text: "Accept it and let it go. That's the whole thing."
options.then: Manav nods slowly. "Okay. That's simpler than I thought."

options.text: "Give them a good reason to change their mind."
options.then: "Like a debate?" Manav says. "I'm good at those."

options.text: "Go quiet and sulk till they feel bad."
options.then: Manav laughs. "Guilt works too, I guess."

steps.why: A no is the answer, not the start of a negotiation.

scenarios.relearn: Calling out 'wearing down' names it as coercion, not romance.

scenarios.hook: Your partner Yash posted a photo of you both, though you'd agreed to keep it offline for now.
scenarios.setup: He calls, cheerful, as the likes come in.

steps.prompt: Yash asks: "Did you see the comments? Everyone loves it!"

options.text: "Yeah, it's cute. Everyone's being so sweet."
options.then: "Right?" Yash says, and posts another one the next day.

options.text: "We agreed to wait. Check with me before, not after."
options.then: Yash's voice drops. "Oh. I thought you'd be happy."

options.text: "Take it down right now, or we're done. Seriously."
options.then: Yash goes silent. "Wow. Okay," he says, stung.

options.text: "It's fine. Just don't tag me in the next one."
options.then: "Deal," Yash says. The agreement you made has shrunk.

steps.why: Naming what you agreed, and asking to be checked with first, resets things fairly.

steps.prompt: Yash says: "My cousin wants to share it in the family group too."

options.text: "Sure, why not. Everyone's seen it anyway."
options.then: "Great," Yash says. By evening, your aunts have seen it.

options.text: "Only if my parents aren't in that group."
options.then: "I don't think so," Yash says. It's out of your hands now.

options.text: "Please don't. It's my picture too, so I get a say."
options.then: Yash pauses. "Okay. I'll tell her no."

options.text: "You never think about anyone but yourself."
options.then: Yash bristles. "That's not fair."

steps.why: Your image is yours. You get a say in where it goes, every time.

steps.prompt: That night, Yash asks: "Is there anything you want me to do differently?"

options.text: "Nothing. Just forget it happened."
options.then: "Cool," he says. The photo stays up.

options.text: "Keep it up, but don't post any more."
options.then: Yash agrees. The photo you didn't agree to stays up.

options.text: "Give me your password so I can check your posts."
options.then: Yash frowns. "That feels like a lot."

options.text: "Take it down, and ask me first next time."
options.then: "Done," Yash says. "And I'll ask. Promise."

steps.why: A clear, fair ask fixes this one and sets the rule for next time.

scenarios.relearn: Asking for 'check before, not after' restores mutual, ongoing consent.

scenarios.hook: At lunch, your classmate Raghav says queer couples don't need the same consent rules.
scenarios.setup: He says it like it's obvious.

steps.prompt: Raghav says: "Two guys just know what the other one wants."

options.text: "Maybe. I haven't really thought about it."
options.then: "Exactly," Raghav says, more sure of himself now.

options.text: "Why are you even talking about gay couples?"
options.then: Raghav shrugs. "Just saying." The idea goes unanswered.

options.text: "Same respect, same consent, for everyone, always."
options.then: Raghav blinks. "Even if they're both guys?"

options.text: "That's so homophobic. You're the worst."
options.then: Raghav gets defensive. "I'm not! I was only saying."

steps.why: The consent standard is identical for every couple. Saying so plainly lands.

steps.prompt: Raghav adds: "I mean, how would it even be pressure between two guys?"

options.text: "Anyone can pressure anyone. A yes must be free."
options.then: Raghav pauses. "Okay. I guess that's true for anyone."

options.text: "Fair point. It's probably pretty rare, honestly."
options.then: "Right," Raghav says. The idea sticks.

options.text: "Ask someone who actually knows about it."
options.then: He shrugs. "Like who?" The question hangs.

options.text: "Why do you care so much about it?"
options.then: Raghav laughs. "I don't. It was just a question."

steps.why: Pressure isn't about gender. Anyone can apply it or face it.

steps.prompt: Raghav asks: "Okay, so what counts as consent, then?"

options.text: "If nobody says no, it's fine."
options.then: "Simple," Raghav says, satisfied.

options.text: "If they're dating, it's kind of understood."
options.then: Raghav nods. "So dating means yes."

options.text: "Look it up yourself. Not my job."
options.then: Raghav rolls his eyes and drops it.

options.text: "A clear, free yes from both, every time."
options.then: Raghav nods. "Huh. Same as for anyone, then."

steps.why: Stating the real standard gives him something true to take away.

scenarios.relearn: The consent standard is identical for everyone, of any orientation.

options.text: "You could at least ask me first, you know."

options.text: "We each say what we'd like, then decide."

options.text: "You plan this one, and I'll plan the next one."

options.text: "Whatever works. I'm sure it'll sort itself out."

options.text: Say love means trust, and ask him to stop
options.then: Aman looks away. "I just get worried," he mutters.

options.text: Wonder aloud what you did to make him doubt you
options.then: Aman nods, as if you've admitted something. You feel guilty for nothing.

options.text: Ask to see his phone too, so it's even
options.then: Aman hands it over. Now you're both checking, and neither of you trusts.

steps.why: Naming snooping as control, not care, is the first step to stopping it.

steps.prompt: Over the next week, Aman starts asking who every message is from. What do you do?

options.text: Decide you must be giving him reasons to worry
options.then: You start deleting harmless chats. The questions don't stop.

options.text: Ask his best friend to get him to back off
options.then: His friend tells Aman. He's angry you 'went behind his back'.

options.text: Tell a trusted adult what's been happening
options.then: The school counsellor listens and says checking up like this is control.

options.text: Tell yourself that all couples do this now
options.then: You shrug it off. The questions keep coming.

steps.why: A trusted adult means you're not alone with this. Being checked on is never your fault.

steps.prompt: Your friend Pooja says all couples check each other's phones these days. What do you say?

options.text: Agree, and wonder if you're overreacting
options.then: You doubt yourself again. Aman's questions feel normal for a day.

options.text: Say Aman's different, because he really loves you
options.then: Pooja smiles. "See? Same thing." The checking feels normal again.

options.text: Say checking up on someone is control, not love
options.then: Pooja thinks, then admits her ex did the same. "I hated it," she says.

options.text: Say it's fine if it only happens now and then
options.then: Pooja nods. The line between care and control blurs.

steps.why: Calling control what it is helps you and your friends see it clearly.

steps.prompt: A month later, Aman says he'll stop checking if you share your location. What do you say?

options.text: Believe sharing it would prove you're loyal
options.then: The idea sits with you. Aman's questions keep coming anyway.

options.text: Ask friends to vouch for wherever you go
options.then: Your friends get pulled in. Aman starts questioning them too.

options.text: Decide it's your fault for having so many friends
options.then: You see friends less. Aman still isn't satisfied.

options.text: Say tracking isn't the fix. Trust is
options.then: Aman goes quiet. You feel clearer about what you won't accept.

steps.why: No amount of proof fixes control. You deserve trust, not tracking.

scenarios.debrief: Checking up on you is control dressed as love; equal partners trust, not surveil.
scenarios.relearn: Checking up on you is control dressed as love; equal partners trust, not surveil.

scenarios.hook: "They bought me dinner, so I kind of owe them."
scenarios.relearn: A gift never creates a debt; intimacy is always a free choice.

myth.un: A paid date or gift means you owe intimacy back.
myth.re: A gift is a gift; nobody is owed intimacy in return for it.
myth.why: Treating intimacy as repayment removes the free 'yes'.

scenarios.hook: "We came all this way to a room, so backing out now would be unfair."
scenarios.relearn: You can stop at any point; effort already spent never owes anyone a yes.

myth.un: Once you've gone somewhere private together, stopping is unfair.
myth.re: You can change your mind anytime; nothing already done owes a yes.
myth.why: An earlier step is not standing consent for the next.

scenarios.hook: "He got so upset and teary that saying no felt cruel."
scenarios.relearn: Someone's hurt feelings are theirs to manage; they never override your no.

myth.un: If refusing makes a partner cry, you should give in to be kind.
myth.re: Their upset is theirs to handle; your 'no' still stands, kindly.
myth.why: Guilt over their reaction is still pressure, not consent.

scenarios.hook: "'Just this once' isn't really pressure, it's just asking."
scenarios.relearn: Pushing again after a no, even softly, is still wearing someone down.

myth.un: Adding 'just this once' makes a repeated ask harmless.
myth.re: Re-asking after a 'no', even softly, is still pressure, not asking.
myth.why: A no already given doesn't need a softer second push.

scenarios.hook: "They didn't say no, so I took it as a green light."
scenarios.relearn: Silence or freezing is not a yes; only a clear, willing yes is.

myth.un: If a partner stays quiet, that counts as agreeing.
myth.re: Silence isn't a yes; without a clear willing yes, you stop.
myth.why: Consent is the presence of a yes, not the absence of a no.

scenarios.hook: "Everyone in our group's already done it, so we're behind."
scenarios.relearn: What others do is never a reason; only your own real yes counts.

myth.un: If friends have all done it, you're behind and should too.
myth.re: Other people's choices aren't a clock; only your own yes counts.
myth.why: Peer pressure replaces your free choice with a crowd's.

scenarios.hook: "They said yes after a few drinks, so it still counts."
scenarios.relearn: Someone who is drunk or high cannot consent; a tipsy 'yes' is not a yes.

myth.un: A yes given while drunk still counts as consent.
myth.re: An incapacitated person can't consent; wait until they're sober.
myth.why: Incapacitation removes the informed, free part of a yes.

scenarios.hook: "In the movies they keep trying and it's romantic, so it works."
scenarios.relearn: Films aren't a script for real life; pushing past a no is coercion, not romance.

myth.un: Persistence is romantic because that's how it looks in films.
myth.re: Real respect waits for a real yes; pushing past a 'no' is coercion.
myth.why: Wearing someone down erases the freely-given part.

scenarios.hook: "We were already kissing, so stopping there made no sense."
scenarios.relearn: A yes to one thing isn't a yes to everything; you can stop at any line.

myth.un: Saying yes to kissing means yes to whatever comes next.
myth.re: Consent is specific; one yes never covers the next thing.
myth.why: Each step needs its own willing yes.

scenarios.hook: "They said they'd break up with me unless I agreed."
scenarios.relearn: An 'agree or we're over' threat makes any yes coercion, not consent.

myth.un: Agreeing to keep a relationship from ending is your free choice.
myth.re: A yes given to dodge a threat isn't consent; that pressure is on them.
myth.why: Threats remove the freely-given part of any yes.

scenarios.hook: "Stopping to check in kills the mood, so it's better to just keep going."
scenarios.relearn: Checking in is warm and normal; the only mood worth keeping is a mutual one.

myth.un: Pausing to ask ruins the moment, so don't bother.
myth.re: Checking in is part of intimacy; pushing past a pause isn't.
myth.why: 'Don't kill the mood' is a line used to skip consent.

scenarios.hook: "A 'good' partner doesn't make a fuss and just goes along."
scenarios.relearn: Going along to seem agreeable isn't a real yes; your willingness is the point.

myth.un: Being agreeable means not making a fuss and just going along.
myth.re: A reluctant 'going along' isn't consent; your real yes is what counts.
myth.why: Pressure to be 'easy-going' is still pressure.

scenarios.hook: "They keep asking for a private photo and say I'm being uptight."
scenarios.relearn: You never owe anyone a photo; 'you're uptight' is pressure, not a fair point.

myth.un: Refusing to send a private photo means you're being uptight.
myth.re: No one is owed a photo; name 'uptight' as the pressure it is.
myth.why: Calling a 'no' uptight is a tactic to flip it to a yes.

scenarios.hook: "I respected their no last time, so this time they kind of owe me."
scenarios.relearn: Respecting a boundary earns no credit toward a future yes.

myth.un: Honouring a 'no' once builds up a yes you can cash in later.
myth.re: A past 'no' you respected owes you nothing now.
myth.why: Decency isn't a transaction that buys future consent.

scenarios.hook: "They waited before telling anyone, so maybe it wasn't that serious."
scenarios.relearn: There's no 'right' time to disclose; a delay never makes harm the survivor's fault.

myth.un: If someone waits to tell, the harm probably wasn't real.
myth.re: People disclose in their own time; a delay never blames the survivor.
myth.why: Doubting a delayed disclosure shifts blame off the wrongdoer.

scenarios.hook: "It's easier to just say yes and avoid a fight."
scenarios.relearn: A yes given only to dodge conflict is pressure-driven, not free.

myth.un: Saying yes to avoid an argument is just keeping the peace.
myth.re: A yes to avoid a fight isn't free; the fight-threat is the pressure.
myth.why: Fear of conflict removes the freely-given part.

scenarios.hook: "They hinted they'd out me to my family unless I agreed."
scenarios.relearn: Threatening to expose someone is blackmail; any yes under it isn't consent.

myth.un: Agreeing so a secret stays safe is just a fair trade.
myth.re: An 'agree or I'll tell' threat is blackmail; that yes isn't consent.
myth.why: Blackmail removes every freely-given part of a choice.

scenarios.hook: "After all the gifts and recharges, surely they should say yes by now."
scenarios.relearn: Spending on someone buys nothing; intimacy is never a return on a gift.

myth.un: Enough gifts and favours eventually earn a yes.
myth.re: Money spent earns no yes; intimacy is never owed in return.
myth.why: Treating a yes as 'earned' erases free choice.

scenarios.hook: You've told Jia you're not ready to go further tonight, but she keeps asking.

steps.prompt: She asks again, for the fourth time. What do you do?

options.text: Wonder if you're being unfair to her
options.then: You feel guilty for having a boundary at all.

options.text: Explain all your reasons again so she understands
options.then: Jia argues with each reason. It turns into a debate about your no.

options.text: Take all the asking as a sign of how much she cares
options.then: It almost feels flattering, until she asks a fifth time.

options.text: Say you've answered, and asking again won't change it
options.then: Jia goes quiet. "Okay. Sorry," she says, a little stiffly.

steps.why: A clear 'I've answered' holds your no without reopening it.

steps.prompt: Next day Jia says she was 'just checking you were sure'. What do you say?

options.text: Say it's fine, since you know she didn't mean it
options.then: Jia smiles, relieved. Next time she asks just as often.

options.text: Say once is checking. Again and again is pressure
options.then: Jia pauses. "I didn't see it that way. Okay."

options.text: Apologise for making things awkward
options.then: Jia accepts. Somehow you're the one who said sorry.

options.text: Say you'll rethink it, to be fair to her
options.then: Jia brightens. Your no now sounds like a maybe.

steps.why: Naming repeated asking as pressure helps her see it, with no blame on you.

steps.prompt: A week later, it happens again. What do you do?

options.text: Hold your no, and tell a trusted adult
options.then: Your aunt listens and says the pushing is Jia's to stop, never your fault.

options.text: Tell yourself every couple has this argument
options.then: You shrug it off. The asking gets more frequent.

options.text: Ask her friends to tell her to stop
options.then: Her friends tease her. Jia is upset that you told them.

options.text: Decide something must be wrong with you
options.then: You feel worse about yourself, though nothing is wrong with you.

steps.why: A pattern of pushing needs support. Re-asking past a no is never your fault.

scenarios.debrief: Re-asking past a clear no is pressure; a firm 'I've answered' holds the line.
scenarios.relearn: Hold your no; re-asking past it is the other person's problem.

scenarios.hook: You're keen to get closer, but tonight Simran seems quieter than usual and a bit unsure.

steps.prompt: She hasn't said stop. What do you do?

options.text: Carry on, since she hasn't actually said stop
options.then: Simran shifts away and goes quiet. The evening turns awkward.

options.text: Ask 'You're fine, right?' and carry on
options.then: Simran says "yeah" automatically. She doesn't sound sure.

options.text: Pause and ask how she's really feeling
options.then: Simran breathes out. "Honestly? I'm tired, and not in the mood."

options.text: Make a joke to lighten her mood
options.then: Simran smiles politely. You still don't know how she feels.

steps.why: No clear yes means pause. Asking openly lets her answer honestly.

steps.prompt: A little later, Simran says she'd rather just talk tonight. What do you say?

options.text: Ask if you did something to upset her
options.then: Simran reassures you. The evening becomes about your feelings.

options.text: Say talking sounds good, and mean it
options.then: Simran relaxes. You end up talking for an hour.

options.text: Say okay, but go quiet and check your phone
options.then: Simran notices. She wonders if she let you down.

options.text: Ask if maybe later tonight could still work
options.then: Simran's face tightens. "I said tonight."

steps.why: Honouring 'not tonight' warmly makes it safe for her to say it again.

steps.prompt: Next day, a friend says you should have 'pushed a bit'. What do you say?

options.text: Say maybe you were too cautious
options.then: Your friend grins. The idea is in your head for next time.

options.text: Laugh, and let the comment pass
options.then: The comment hangs there, unanswered.

options.text: Tell him every detail so he can judge
options.then: You share more than Simran would want. It feels like a betrayal.

options.text: Say if she's unsure, the answer is wait
options.then: Your friend shrugs. "Fair. I guess."

steps.why: Saying it out loud keeps you clear: unsure means wait, not push.

scenarios.debrief: When enthusiasm dips, the move is to pause and check, not push on.
scenarios.relearn: If a partner seems unsure, pause and check; don't push on.

scenarios.hook: You've just said no to your partner Rehan. He sighs: "I guess you don't really care about us."

steps.prompt: He waits for your answer. What do you do?

options.text: Wonder if he's right that you don't care enough
options.then: The guilt sits in your chest all evening.

options.text: Name it as a guilt-trip, and keep your answer
options.then: Rehan looks away. "Wow. Okay," he mutters.

options.text: Reassure him at length about how much you care
options.then: Rehan listens, then says, "So prove it."

options.text: Believe that real love means saying yes
options.then: The idea unsettles you. Your no feels shakier.

steps.why: Naming a guilt-trip strips its power. Your no still stands.

steps.prompt: Later, Rehan sends a long message about how hurt he is. What do you do?

options.text: Apologise for hurting him so badly
options.then: Rehan replies warmly. Next time, he uses the same line.

options.text: Ask a friend to message him and explain
options.then: Your friend's message makes Rehan angrier.

options.text: Write a long reply defending every reason
options.then: Rehan answers each point. It goes on past midnight.

options.text: Reply that his hurt is his, and your no stands
options.then: Rehan sends a short 'fine'. The pressure has nowhere to land.

steps.why: You can care about his feelings without them deciding for you.

steps.prompt: A few days later, he says it again. What do you do?

options.text: Decide you must be cold, since he keeps saying it
options.then: You start doubting yourself in other ways too.

options.text: Talk to a trusted adult about the guilt-trips
options.then: Your mum listens and says the pressure is his doing, never yours.

options.text: Tell yourself all couples guilt each other a bit
options.then: You let it pass. The line keeps coming back.

options.text: Promise to make it up to him another way
options.then: Rehan smiles. Your no has become something to repay.

steps.why: A trusted adult helps you hold firm. Being guilt-tripped is never your fault.

scenarios.debrief: Naming a guilt-trip out loud strips its power; your no still stands.
scenarios.relearn: Name a guilt-trip out loud; it loses its grip when you do.

scenarios.hook: Between classes, your classmate Neha quietly tells you her ex forced her.

steps.prompt: She's shaking. What do you say first?

options.text: Ask her exactly what happened, step by step
options.then: Neha's voice shakes. She stops halfway and looks away.

options.text: Ask why she didn't tell anyone sooner
options.then: Neha shrinks. "I don't know. I'm sorry."

options.text: Say you'll find her ex and sort them out
options.then: Neha panics. "No! Please don't do anything."

options.text: Say you believe her, and it wasn't her fault
options.then: Neha's breath catches. "You believe me?" she whispers.

steps.why: Belief and 'not your fault' come first. They tell her she's safe with you.

steps.prompt: Neha begs you to promise you won't tell anyone. What do you say?

options.text: Promise, so that she keeps on trusting you
options.then: Neha relaxes. You're left holding something too big alone.

options.text: Say you can't promise that, but you won't leave her
options.then: Neha looks scared, then nods. "Just stay with me."

options.text: Say you're going to tell the principal right now
options.then: Neha backs away. "No. Not like that," she whispers.

options.text: Tell her to try to move on and forget it
options.then: Neha nods, but her face closes off.

steps.why: You can't keep a secret that leaves her at risk, but you can stay beside her.

steps.prompt: Next day, Neha finds you and asks who she could even talk to. What do you say?

options.text: Say only her parents can really deal with this
options.then: Neha shakes her head. "I can't tell them. Not yet."

options.text: Suggest the counsellor or Childline 1098, with you
options.then: Neha nods slowly. "Maybe the counsellor. If you come."

options.text: Say she'll need proof before anyone believes her
options.then: Neha's face falls. "Then no one will believe me."

options.text: Search online together for what she should do now
options.then: You find lists of numbers. Neha feels more overwhelmed.

steps.why: Real help, offered at her pace with you there, makes reaching out possible.

steps.prompt: That evening, what she told you weighs on you. What do you do?

options.text: Post a vague story about it so people know
options.then: Classmates start guessing. Neha sees it and feels exposed.

options.text: Keep it to yourself, so you don't betray her trust
options.then: You can't sleep. You don't know how to help her on your own.

options.text: Talk to a trusted adult about how to help Neha
options.then: Your aunt listens quietly, then helps you plan how to get Neha support.

options.text: Text Neha every hour to check she's okay
options.then: Neha mutes the chat. It feels like too much.

steps.why: You need support too. A trusted adult can help you get Neha real help.

steps.prompt: A week later, Neha says it feels like her fault for dating her ex. What do you say?

options.text: Say dating someone is never a yes. It wasn't her fault
options.then: Neha breathes out. "I keep needing to hear that."

options.text: Say she'll just need to be more careful next time
options.then: Neha's face falls. "So it was my fault."

options.text: Say she should just try to forget about her ex
options.then: Neha nods, but the guilt stays.

options.text: Change the subject to cheer her up
options.then: Neha smiles briefly. The guilt goes unsaid.

steps.why: Self-blame needs a clear answer: what happened was never her fault.

scenarios.debrief: A disclosure of force routes to help: believe them, no blame, Childline 1098.
scenarios.relearn: Believe a disclosure, never blame them, and route to real help.

scenarios.hook: Someone you used to chat with threatens to share an old private photo unless you meet them.

steps.prompt: Their message says you have until tonight. What do you do?

options.text: Ask a friend, who says meeting once will make them delete it
options.then: It feels like a way out, but their messages promise nothing.

options.text: Tell yourself it's your fault for sending the photo
options.then: Shame floods in. It makes it harder to think about who could help.

options.text: Refuse, and screenshot the messages
options.then: They send angry replies. You have every one of them saved.

options.text: Threaten to report them, so they back off
options.then: They laugh and send another threat.

steps.why: Refusing and saving proof keeps you in charge. Blackmail is never your fault.

steps.prompt: That evening, it's all you can think about. What do you do?

options.text: Ask strangers online how to handle it
options.then: Strangers give mixed advice. One says just meet them.

options.text: Tell a trusted adult what's happening
options.then: Your dad stays calm. "Thank you for telling me. We'll sort this together."

options.text: Ask a friend to message them pretending to be you
options.then: Your friend's message makes them angrier, and more threats arrive.

options.text: Try to find out who else they've done this to
options.then: You spend hours digging, and the deadline gets closer.

steps.why: A trusted adult can help you act. You don't have to face this alone.

steps.prompt: The next day, a new account sends the same threat. What do you do?

options.text: Believe it's too late, since they still have the photo
options.then: You feel trapped, as if the photo decides everything.

options.text: Reply angrily to show you're not scared
options.then: They screenshot your reply and send more threats.

options.text: Save it too, and report the account with an adult's help
options.then: The report goes in. You feel less alone with it.

options.text: Tell yourself they're probably just bluffing
options.then: You try to ignore it, but keep checking your phone.

steps.why: Reporting, with help, takes the power out of the threat.

steps.prompt: Weeks later, a friend admits someone is threatening her with a photo. What do you do?

options.text: Ask her why she sent the photo in the first place
options.then: She shuts down. "I knew you'd say that."

options.text: Tell her to just do what they want so it ends
options.then: She looks more frightened than before.

options.text: Say it's not her fault, and help her tell an adult
options.then: She cries with relief. "I thought I'd be in trouble."

options.text: Promise to keep it a secret between you two
options.then: She thanks you. You both carry it alone.

steps.why: Blame never helps. Belief and a trusted adult do.

scenarios.debrief: Threatening to share a photo is blackmail; refuse and tell a trusted adult.
scenarios.relearn: Photo threats are blackmail; refuse and tell someone you trust.

scenarios.hook: You notice you keep telling Neil 'come on, don't overthink it' whenever he hesitates.

steps.prompt: He hesitates again tonight. What do you do?

options.text: Say it again, but more gently this time
options.then: Neil laughs nervously and changes the topic.

options.text: Keep nudging. He'll relax soon enough
options.then: Neil goes quiet and checks his phone.

options.text: Stop, and tell him there's zero rush from you
options.then: Neil's shoulders drop. "Really? Okay. Thanks."

options.text: Say nothing, but look a bit disappointed
options.then: Neil notices, and apologises without knowing what for.

steps.why: Saying there's no rush takes the pressure off and keeps it his call.

steps.prompt: Next day, 'don't overthink it' is on your lips again. What do you do?

options.text: Say it anyway. It's only a phrase
options.then: The phrase lands on Neil as a push again.

options.text: Feel so guilty you avoid getting close at all
options.then: Neil wonders why you've gone cold on him.

options.text: Ask a friend if it's really that bad
options.then: Your friend says it's fine. Neil's hesitation says otherwise.

options.text: Drop the line, and ask how he feels instead
options.then: Next time, Neil tells you what he's comfortable with.

steps.why: Swapping a push for a real question makes his answer free.

steps.prompt: A week later, Neil tells you how that line makes him feel. What do you say?

options.text: Say sorry, and that his pace leads from now on
options.then: Neil smiles. "I didn't think you'd take it so well."

options.text: Say you were only joking around
options.then: Neil nods, but looks unconvinced.

options.text: Say he should have told you sooner
options.then: Neil looks hurt. "I didn't feel like I could."

options.text: Say sorry, but that he's a bit oversensitive
options.then: Neil's face falls. "So it's my fault for feeling it?"

steps.why: Owning it and letting his pace lead keeps trust equal.

scenarios.debrief: Being even-handed means catching your own nudging and stopping it.
scenarios.relearn: Catch your own nudging; tell a hesitant partner there's no rush.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Yuvraj says his girlfriend sulks for days when he says no, so he just gives in.

steps.prompt: He shrugs it off as normal. What do you say?

options.text: Say all couples have to compromise on things sometimes
options.then: Yuvraj nods. "Yeah. That's what I tell myself."

options.text: Tell him to just break up with her
options.then: Yuvraj bristles. "It's not that simple."

options.text: Say a yes to end sulking isn't owed. You're with him
options.then: Yuvraj goes quiet. "I never thought of it as pressure."

options.text: Joke that guys can't really be pressured
options.then: Yuvraj laughs too, but stops talking about it.

steps.why: Naming sulking as pressure, and backing him, takes the guilt off him.

steps.prompt: Yuvraj asks you not to tell anyone, since it's embarrassing. What do you say?

options.text: Promise to keep it strictly between the two of you
options.then: Yuvraj relaxes. You're left worried, unsure how to help.

options.text: Say there's no shame, and offer the counsellor together
options.then: Yuvraj hesitates. "Maybe. If you come too."

options.text: Say you'll tell his parents for him, so he doesn't have to
options.then: Yuvraj looks horrified and stops replying.

options.text: Agree it's embarrassing, so keep it quiet
options.then: Yuvraj nods. The shame stays with him.

steps.why: There's no shame in being pressured, and an adult can help.

steps.prompt: A week later, Yuvraj says she sulked again when he said no. What do you do?

options.text: Suggest he give in once to keep things calm
options.then: Yuvraj looks tired. "That's what I always do."

options.text: Tell him to sulk right back so she sees how it feels
options.then: Yuvraj laughs, but it doesn't help.

options.text: Message his girlfriend to tell her off
options.then: She's furious, and Yuvraj is caught in the middle.

options.text: Say it's not his fault. Help him get to the counsellor
options.then: Yuvraj nods. "Okay. Let's go after class."

steps.why: Her sulking is hers to own. It's never his fault, and help is close by.

steps.prompt: Later, Yuvraj asks if he's 'weak' for giving in before. What do you say?

options.text: Say a bit, and he should've stood up for himself
options.then: Yuvraj looks down. "Yeah. I guess."

options.text: Say no. Giving in under pressure is never his fault
options.then: Yuvraj's eyes fill. "I really needed to hear that."

options.text: Say guys are expected to want it, so it's confusing
options.then: Yuvraj frowns. "So something's wrong with me?"

options.text: Say let's not dwell on the past
options.then: Yuvraj nods, but the question stays with him.

steps.why: Giving in under pressure is never partly his fault. Saying so lifts the shame.

scenarios.debrief: Sulking until someone gives in is coercion; a friend can name it and back them.
scenarios.relearn: Back a pressured friend: a yes to stop sulking is never owed.

scenarios.hook: At a party, your partner Isha has had a lot to drink. She leans in: "Let's go somewhere."

steps.prompt: She's swaying a little. What do you do?

options.text: Go with her, since she's the one asking
options.then: Isha trips on the stairs. She can barely stand.

options.text: Say maybe in an hour, after some water
options.then: Isha grins. "An hour, then," she says, still slurring.

options.text: Laugh it off and leave her with her friends

steps.why: Naming blackmail takes its power away. Refusing is always allowed, and it's never your fault.

steps.prompt: Dev texts again: "Think about it. Everyone at school will laugh at you."

options.text: "You're right. No one at school would take my side."
options.then: "Exactly," he writes. "So stop acting brave."

options.text: "I'm saving these messages. My answer is still no."
options.then: A long pause. Then: "Saving them? Why would you do that?"

options.text: "Fine, post it. I honestly don't care anymore."
options.then: "We'll see," he replies. "Tomorrow, then."

options.text: "Why are you doing this? I thought you cared."
options.then: "I do care," he writes. "That's why I want you back."

steps.why: Saved messages are proof, and proof helps the adults who step in.

steps.prompt: At lunch, your friend Tanvi asks: "You've been glued to your phone. What's wrong?"

options.text: "Dev's threatening me. It's my fault for trusting him."

options.text: "Help me find something on Dev so I can hit back at him."

options.text: "Dev's threatening to out me. I want to tell an adult."
options.then: Tanvi squeezes your arm. "I'll come with you. Today."

options.text: "Can you and the others go and scare Dev off?"
options.then: "A fight?" Tanvi asks. "That gets us all in trouble."

steps.why: A friend's support helps, and an adult can actually stop this.

steps.prompt: That night your mother finds you awake and asks: "What's keeping you up?"

options.text: "Is this my fault, Ma, for being out at home?"
options.then: She holds your hand. "Never. Now tell me what's happened."

options.text: "Can you call Dev's parents right now and yell at them?"
options.then: "At midnight?" she asks. "First tell me what's going on."

options.text: "Promise you'll get Dev thrown out of school."
options.then: "I can't promise that," she says gently. "But I'm listening."

options.text: "Dev says he'll out me at school. I need your help."
options.then: She sits on the bed. "Thank you for telling me. We'll handle this together."

steps.why: A trusted adult can protect you. Childline 1098 can help too, any time.

steps.prompt: Two days later Dev texts: "Okay, maybe I won't post. If you're nice to me."

options.text: "My family knows now. Don't contact me again."
options.then: "Wow. Okay," he replies. Then nothing more.

options.text: "Why should I believe anything you say?"
options.then: "You don't have to," he replies. "Just be nice."

options.text: "Prove it. Delete everything and send me screenshots."
options.then: "Maybe," he writes. "If you're nice first."

options.text: "Post anything and you'll regret it."
options.then: "Is that a threat?" he replies. "Screenshotting this."

steps.why: Help is on your side now. You don't owe Dev a deal, or a reply.
