scenarios.hook: Things are moving faster than usual with Bhavna, and you want to make sure you're both in.
scenarios.setup: You're sitting close on her sofa after a film.

steps.prompt: Bhavna laughs and says: "Wow, okay."

options.text: "Too fast? Ha. You seem to be enjoying it."
options.then: Bhavna's laugh fades. "I mean... I don't know."

options.text: "Sorry. I'll stop right now if you want."
options.then: Bhavna hesitates. "I didn't say stop. I just..."

options.text: "Are you happy with this? We can slow down."
options.then: Bhavna takes a breath and thinks about it.

options.text: "Just relax. Go with it."
options.then: Bhavna nods, but she goes quieter.

steps.why: Asking if she's happy, with slowing down on offer, makes consent clear and shared.

steps.prompt: Bhavna says: "Honestly? A bit slower would be nice."

options.text: "Okay, but we were having fun."
options.then: Bhavna's smile fades. "I still am. Just slower."

options.text: "Sure. Thanks for saying so."
options.then: Bhavna smiles and settles back against you.

options.text: "Slower? Did I do something wrong?"
options.then: Bhavna ends up reassuring you.

options.text: "Okay. Just say when to speed up again."
options.then: Bhavna nods, as if speeding up is now her job.

steps.why: Thanking her for speaking up makes the next check-in even easier.

steps.prompt: Later, Bhavna asks: "How do you usually know if someone's into it?"

options.text: "I can usually just tell from their face."
options.then: Bhavna nods. "And if you can't tell?"

options.text: "If they don't say stop, they're into it."
options.then: Bhavna frowns. "That's not always true."

options.text: "I ask once at the start, then relax."
options.then: Bhavna nods. "So after that, you just assume?"

options.text: "I ask. And I want you to ask me too."
options.then: Bhavna grins. "Deal. Both ways."

steps.why: Asking, both ways, is how you know. It keeps consent shared every time.

scenarios.relearn: Asking 'are you happy with this?' makes consent clear and shared.

scenarios.hook: You said yes to kissing Kartik earlier, but now you're not feeling it.
scenarios.setup: You're sitting close on the bench outside his building.

steps.prompt: Kartik asks: "You okay? You've gone quiet."

options.text: "I'm fine. Just thinking about tomorrow's test."
options.then: Kartik nods slowly. "You seem far away, though."

options.text: "I know I said yes, but I want to stop now."
options.then: Kartik moves back a little. "Okay. Thanks for telling me."

options.text: "Sorry. I'm being so difficult today."
options.then: Kartik frowns. "Difficult? What do you mean?"

options.text: "I said yes, so I should be fine, right?"
options.then: Kartik pauses. "You don't have to be fine. What's up?"

steps.why: An earlier yes isn't binding. You can say "I want to stop now" at any moment.

steps.prompt: Kartik asks: "Was it something I did?"

options.text: "No. I'll tell you why once I know."
options.then: Kartik nods, and you feel you owe him an answer later.

options.text: "I don't know. Maybe I'm just weird."
options.then: Kartik shakes his head. "You're not weird."

options.text: "No. I just don't want to right now."
options.then: Kartik nods. "Okay. Do you want to walk for a bit?"

options.text: "Yes. You should have noticed sooner."
options.then: Kartik looks stung. "I'm sorry. I didn't know."

steps.why: You don't owe a reason. A simple "I don't want to right now" is enough.

steps.prompt: Later, Kartik says: "I never want you doing anything you don't want."

options.text: "Can we not make it a big thing?"
options.then: Kartik nods, and the moment to talk passes.

options.text: "Don't worry. Next time I'll be more in the mood."
options.then: Kartik pauses. "You don't have to promise that."

options.text: "Thanks. I'll always tell you, and you tell me too."
options.then: Kartik smiles. "Deal. Both ways."

options.text: "Sure. As long as you're not upset."
options.then: Kartik shakes his head. "I'm not. That's not the point."

steps.why: Agreeing to keep speaking up, both ways, makes stopping feel normal between you.

steps.prompt: Later, your friend Muskaan says: "If you've said yes, you can't really back out after."

options.text: "You can. A yes can be taken back anytime."
options.then: Muskaan pauses. "Huh. I really didn't know that."

options.text: "Only if you have a good reason."
options.then: Muskaan nods. "So you have to justify it."

options.text: "Maybe. It's awkward to back out."
options.then: Muskaan nods. "Right. So better not to."

options.text: "I guess it depends on the person and the situation."
options.then: Muskaan shrugs, and her idea doesn't change.

steps.why: Consent is reversible. An earlier yes never traps anyone.

scenarios.relearn: An earlier yes isn't binding; you can say 'I want to stop now' anytime.

steps.why: A yes to one thing isn't a yes to the next. Each step needs its own yes.

steps.prompt: Jasleen says she'd like to keep things to kissing for now. What do you do?

options.text: Ask when she thinks she'll be ready for more
options.then: Jasleen shrugs, feeling she has to give you a date.

options.text: Agree, but go a bit quiet
options.then: Jasleen notices and starts to feel guilty.

options.text: Say "Sure," and keep it just as it is
options.then: Jasleen smiles and leans into you.

options.text: Tell her you thought she was enjoying it
options.then: Jasleen frowns. "I am. That's why I want this."

steps.why: Honouring her "for now" straight away, with no sulk or timeline, keeps her yes free.

steps.prompt: A few weeks later, Jasleen says she'd like to cuddle as well as kiss. What do you do?

options.text: Take it as a yes to everything from now on
options.then: Jasleen hesitates. "I didn't say everything."

options.text: Ask if she's really sure, since she said not yet before
options.then: Jasleen frowns. "I'm sure. I changed my mind."

options.text: Say you'd like that, and keep checking in as you go
options.then: Jasleen nods. "Yes. And you tell me too."

options.text: Ask a friend what usually comes next
options.then: Your friend shares opinions that have nothing to do with Jasleen.

steps.why: A yes to cuddling covers cuddling. Checking in as you go keeps it hers too.

steps.prompt: Your friend Tanvi says a happy yes once means "the rest is implied." What do you tell her?

options.text: "Only if you're already in a relationship."
options.then: Tanvi nods. "So couples can skip asking."

options.text: "No. A yes covers one thing at a time."
options.then: Tanvi thinks. "So a kiss isn't a yes to everything."

options.text: "Sort of, unless they stop you."
options.then: Tanvi nods. "So it's on them to stop it."

options.text: "It's different for everyone."
options.then: Tanvi shrugs, and her idea stays the same.

steps.why: Consent is specific. A yes to one step never covers the next.

scenarios.debrief: Consent is specific; a yes to one step never covers the next.
scenarios.relearn: Each new step needs its own yes; one yes isn't a yes to all.

scenarios.hook: You said yes to kissing Abhay, but now you'd rather stop.

steps.prompt: Abhay hasn't noticed anything has changed for you. What do you do?

options.text: Tell yourself you can't back out after saying yes
options.then: The thought weighs on you, until Abhay notices and pauses to ask.

options.text: Apologise first for leading him on
options.then: Abhay stops, confused. "Led me on? You don't owe me anything."

options.text: Tell him: "I've changed my mind. Let's stop."
options.then: Abhay pulls back at once. "Okay. You alright?"

options.text: Say you're tired, so it sounds less awkward
options.then: Abhay stops. "Oh, okay. Another time, then?"

steps.why: An earlier yes never traps you. You can stop anytime, no reason owed.

steps.prompt: Abhay asks if he did something wrong. What do you say?

options.text: "No, it's me. I'm being weird."
options.then: Abhay shakes his head. "You're not being weird."

options.text: "No. I just don't want to anymore."
options.then: Abhay nods. "Okay. Thanks for telling me."

options.text: "Kind of. You should have noticed."
options.then: Abhay looks hurt. "I'm sorry. I didn't know."

options.text: "No. I'll explain once I figure it out."
options.then: Abhay nods, and you start worrying about what you'll say.

steps.why: You don't need a reason to stop. "I don't want to anymore" is enough.

steps.prompt: Later, a thought nags at you: maybe you shouldn't have said yes at all. What do you tell yourself?

options.text: "Next time, I won't say yes unless I'm certain."
options.then: You feel the pressure of never being allowed to change your mind.

options.text: "I probably confused him. That's on me."
options.then: The guilt follows you all the way home.

options.text: "Saying yes then and stopping now were both okay."
options.then: The knot in your stomach slowly loosens.

options.text: "I'll make it up to him next time."
options.then: A debt you never owed starts to take shape in your head.

steps.why: Changing your mind isn't a mistake. Consent is reversible, every time.

steps.prompt: Your friend Rukhsar says stopping after a yes is "unfair" to the other person. What do you tell her?

options.text: "True. You should be sure before you start."
options.then: Rukhsar nods. "Right. Once you start, you finish."

options.text: "Only if you stop for no reason."
options.then: Rukhsar nods. "So you need a good reason to stop."

options.text: "It depends how far you've gone."
options.then: Rukhsar nods. "So there's a point of no return."

options.text: "A yes can be taken back anytime. That's fair."
options.then: Rukhsar thinks. "Huh. So a yes isn't a promise."

steps.why: Consent is reversible. Stopping is always fair, whenever you want to.

scenarios.debrief: Consent is reversible; changing your mind is always allowed, no reason owed.
scenarios.relearn: You can withdraw a yes anytime; an earlier yes never traps you.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Rohit says he's dating someone, so he doesn't really need to ask each time.

steps.prompt: He sounds very sure of himself. What do you say?

options.text: "Yeah. Once you're together, it's mostly fine."
options.then: Rohit nods, satisfied. "That's what I thought."

options.text: "Only ask if they seem unsure."
options.then: Rohit nods. "So if they seem fine, skip it."

options.text: "You do, though. Dating isn't a standing yes."
options.then: Rohit frowns. "Really? Even after months?"

options.text: "Your relationship, your business."
options.then: Rohit shrugs, and the idea stays put.

steps.why: No relationship replaces a clear, willing yes, each time.

steps.prompt: Rohit says asking every time would feel "weird" after months together. What do you say?

options.text: "It can be simple, like 'Is this good?'"
options.then: Rohit laughs. "Okay, that's less weird than I thought."

options.text: "Then just read their face. That works too."
options.then: Rohit nods. "Right, faces. Easy."

options.text: "Maybe ask once at the start of the evening."
options.then: Rohit nods. "Once an evening. Got it."

options.text: "Yeah, it would be weird. Never mind."
options.then: Rohit grins, and nothing changes.

steps.why: Checking in can be quick and natural, even after months together.

steps.prompt: Rohit asks what happens if his partner says yes to one thing but not another. What do you tell him?

options.text: "Try again later. They might change their mind."
options.then: Rohit nods. "So keep asking till it's yes."

options.text: "Talk them into it, gently."
options.then: Rohit nods. "Gently. Right."

options.text: "Ask why, so you understand them better."
options.then: Rohit nods. "So they should explain themselves."

options.text: "Then that's the answer. Each needs its own yes."
options.then: Rohit nods slowly. "Okay. That's actually clear."

steps.why: A yes is specific. A no to one thing is respected straight away.

steps.prompt: A week later, Rohit says his partner thanked him for asking. What do you say?

options.text: "See? Now you can stop asking."
options.then: Rohit pauses. "Wait, I thought I should keep asking."

options.text: "That's what a yes from both of you feels like."
options.then: Rohit grins. "It did feel better."

options.text: "Nice. Maybe just ask for the big things from now on."
options.then: Rohit nods. "Big things only. Okay."

options.text: "Cool. Don't overdo it, though."
options.then: Rohit shrugs, unsure how much is too much.

steps.why: Asking every time keeps consent shared, however long you've been together.

scenarios.debrief: No relationship status replaces a clear, willing yes for each time.
scenarios.relearn: Dating isn't standing consent; each time still needs a real yes.

scenarios.hook: Your partner Harleen tells you: "Only if you really want to. No pressure."

steps.prompt: You're not sure yet what you want. What do you do?

options.text: Take it as a hint that you should say yes
options.then: You say yes quickly, and Harleen smiles, not knowing you're unsure.

options.text: Take it as real care, and answer honestly
options.then: Harleen nods when you say you're unsure. "That's completely fine."

options.text: Say "I don't know" and change the subject
options.then: Harleen nods, and the question hangs between you.

options.text: Ask her what she wants first
options.then: Harleen smiles. "I asked you first."

steps.why: "No pressure" means your honest answer is welcome, whatever it is.

steps.prompt: Later, Harleen says she'd hate for you to ever agree just to please her. What do you say?

options.text: "That would never happen. Don't worry."
options.then: Harleen nods, though she doesn't look convinced.

options.text: "I'll tell you honestly. And keep asking me too."
options.then: Harleen squeezes your hand. "Deal. I want the real you."

options.text: "Even if I did, it's no big deal."
options.then: Harleen pauses. "It is to me."

options.text: "I'll try to want whatever you want, then."
options.then: Harleen looks sad. "That's not what I'm asking for."

steps.why: Going along isn't a failing. Saying what's true, with her checking too, keeps every yes real.

steps.prompt: Your friend Ritika says when someone says "no pressure," they secretly want a yes. What do you tell her?

options.text: "Sometimes. You have to read between the lines."
options.then: Ritika nods. "Right. So say yes, to be safe."

options.text: "True. That's why I usually say yes."
options.then: Ritika laughs. "Same, honestly."

options.text: "It means exactly that. Answer for yourself."
options.then: Ritika nods. "So you really are allowed to say no."

options.text: "It depends on who says it."
options.then: Ritika nods, still unsure when to trust it.

steps.why: Consent is freely given. When someone means no pressure, your honest no is welcome.

scenarios.debrief: A real 'no pressure' frees you to give an honest yes or no; that's the point.
scenarios.relearn: Consent is freely given; 'no pressure' means your honest answer is welcome.
